relations.subject: server:collections-manifest
relations.evidence: The `manifest_uid` value is associated with the current state of collections on the node; and will be incremented whenever a collections-related change is made.

relations.subject: server:collection-change-history
relations.evidence: the value can only be `true` when _Magma_ has been configured as the storage engine for the bucket

relations.subject: server:collection
relations.evidence: This command is used to provide low-level details on collections, for a specified bucket. This includes details identifying the existing collections; and vBucket-specific details, which include sequence numbers and item counts.

notable_absence.finding: As with cbstats-collections.md, no privilege or role is ever named for running this command - only demonstrated by example ('-u Administrator -p password').

cross_component_finding: Two things stand out for authorship provenance on this specific page. First, the manifest_uid explanatory sentence and the Magma-gated history sentence are BOTH reproduced here word-for-word (bar 'The' vs 'The collection's' at the start of the history sentence) from cbstats-collections.md - confirming the copy-paste hypothesis in the surrounding prose. Second, the example response block contains what reads as an unedited raw-terminal-dump artifact: two lines run stat names together with no separating whitespace or line break - `vb_8:manifest:uidvb_8:default_mvs:` and `vb_8:manifest:uidvb_8:default_mvsvb_8:default_legacy_max_dcp_seqno:` - evidence the sample output was pasted directly from a tool's stdout and never proofread for line-wrapping errors, distinct from and additional to the prose-level copy-paste. The underlying STATS THEMSELVES, however, are genuinely deeper here than on cbstats-collections.md (per-vBucket disk_size/high_seqno/persisted_high_seqno/start_seqno breakdowns, absent from the base page) - so the base/-details pair is copy-pasted in its explanatory prose but not redundant in its actual data.
cross_product_finding: No Capella analog for this level of per-vBucket-per-collection detail; Capella's collection surface has no manifest_uid or change-history equivalent.
